issues.body: `a_closed_downstream_pipe_is_a_quiet_exit` runs the pipeline with `Command::new("sh")` but uses `${PIPESTATUS[0]}`, which is a Bash array and is unsupported by common `/bin/sh` implementations such as dash. More importantly, the test never asserts `out.status.success()` (or any expected status); it only checks that stderr lacks the word `panicked`. A shell `Bad substitution` failure therefore passes the test, as can other failures that never exercise the intended CLI behavior. This leaves the only test for the newly documented quiet broken-pipe exit unable to catch a regression.
issues.fix_hint: Run an explicitly supported shell (for example `bash -o pipefail -c ...`) and assert the command status is successful, or avoid a shell by wiring the child stdout to a pipe whose read end is closed and asserting the CLI process exits with status 0. Also assert stderr is empty or otherwise matches the intended quiet behavior.
issues.title: Broken-pipe test does not verify the CLI exits successfully

verdict.summary: The streaming implementation is broadly coherent and the HTTP tests exercise the principal response paths, but the CLI broken-pipe regression test is vacuous on common test hosts. It invokes a Bash-only PIPESTATUS array through `sh`, then neither requires the pipeline command to succeed nor verifies the CLI exit status. Consequently the test can pass because the shell itself reports a substitution error, without ever establishing the documented quiet-success behavior.
